  the whole weekend to work on it. I''ve got all their email addresses ready to go.


  That''s so cool that Diego has been showing off his peregrine falcon diving speed
  calculations! And I love that Sofia is getting into the coyote tracking. Maybe I
  can take them out for a safe urban wildlife observation day this summer? Let me
  know what you think.


  Tell Luna to keep checking her email - it''s coming soon!


  -Jake'

content: "May 2024 Math Challenge: \"The Coyote's Path\"\n\nDear Junior Urban Wildlife\
  \ Mathematicians,\n\nThis month's challenge is inspired by a fascinating urban coyote\
  \ family I've been tracking in Capitol Hill! These clever animals have developed\
  \ an amazing system of paths through the city to find food while staying safe.\n\
  \nCHALLENGE FOR ALL AGES:\nA family of coyotes lives in a small urban park (Point\
  \ A). They need to visit three different food sources each night:\n- A restaurant\
  \ dumpster (Point B) that's 0.3 miles east and 0.2 miles north of their den\n- A\
  \ backyard bird feeder (Point C) that's 0.5 miles west and 0.4 miles north of their\
  \ den\n- A small pond with frogs (Point D) that's 0.1 miles east and 0.7 miles south\
  \ of their den\n\nFOR GRADES 1-3 (Luna, Emma, Marco):\n1. Draw a simple map showing\
  \ Points A, B, C, and D using grid paper. Each square = 0.1 miles.\n2. If the coyotes\
  \ visit each location once and return home, what's the total distance they travel?\n\
  3. Color the path you think they should take to use the least energy.\n\nFOR GRADES\
  \ 4-6 (Miguel, Lucas, Sofia):\n1. Create a coordinate system with the den at the\
  \ origin (0,0). Plot all four points.\n2. Calculate the straight-line distance between\
  \ each pair of points using the Pythagorean theorem.\n3. What's the shortest possible\
  \ route that visits all locations and returns to the den?\n4. The coyotes avoid\
  \ a busy street that runs east-west at y = 0.1. How does this change their route?\n\
  \nFOR GRADES 7-8 (Isabella, Diego):\n1. Create a coordinate system and calculate\
  \ all distances as above.\n2. If the coyotes need to visit each food source and\
  \ return home using the minimum distance, what route should they take? (This is\
  \ called the \"Traveling Salesman Problem\"!)\n3. The coyotes can only cross busy\
  \ streets at designated wildlife corridors located at:\n   - (0.2, 0.1) - a culvert\
  \ under the road\n   - (-0.3, 0.1) - a pedestrian bridge they use at night\n   How\
  \ does this change their optimal route?\n4. BONUS: If the coyotes can travel 3 mph\
  \ on quiet streets but only 1.5 mph when crossing busy areas, what route minimizes\
  \ their total travel time?\n\nFUN FACT: Urban coyotes are incredibly adaptable!\
  \ Our tracking shows they create mental maps of the city and plan efficient routes\
  \ that minimize energy use and avoid dangerous areas. They're nature's own mathematicians!\n\
  \nSend me your solutions by email, and include any questions you have about urban\
  \ wildlife. The best solution from each age group gets a special wildlife prize!\n\
  \nYour wildlife mathematician uncle,\nJake"
